questions.q: How is Append different from Merge?
options: Append stacks rows from tables that share columns; Merge combines columns from tables that share a key
They are two names for the exact same operation
Append only works with numeric columns
Merge can only combine two tables; Append can combine any number
questions.explain: Append reaches downward, stacking rows underneath each other. Merge reaches sideways, pulling matching columns in based on a shared key column.

questions.q: Two tables are appended, but only one of them has a "Referrer" column. What happens to the Referrer values for rows from the other table?
options: They show null — not an error, just a column that table never had
Power Query refuses to append the tables at all
The rows from the table without Referrer are silently dropped
Power Query invents placeholder Referrer values
questions.explain: Every column from every appended table survives in the result. Rows from a table that never had a given column simply show null there — expected behavior, not an error.

questions.q: Does Power Query match columns by name or by position when appending?
options: By name
By position (column order)
By data type only
Columns must be manually mapped every time
questions.explain: Power Query matches columns by their header name across the appended tables, not by which position they happen to occupy in each table.

questions.q: What's the difference between "Append queries" and "Append queries as new"?
options: Append queries adds rows into your current query; Append queries as new creates a separate new query, leaving the originals untouched
They produce different column matching behavior
Append queries as new only works with three or more tables
There is no difference
questions.explain: "Append queries" modifies your currently selected query in place. "Append queries as new" builds a brand-new query instead, so both original queries remain unchanged.

questions.q: When would you use "Three or more tables" mode instead of appending pairs one at a time?
options: When combining several similarly-shaped tables at once, like monthly exports or regional files
It's required for every append operation
Only when the tables have completely different columns
Three or more tables mode doesn't actually exist in Power Query Desktop
questions.explain: Three or more tables mode lets you build a list of tables to combine in one step — the natural choice when you have several similarly-shaped sources to stack together.
